newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U drops on report, '97 outlook.
newsitem.headline: P&U drops on report, '97 outlook.

text.p: Swedish/U.S. drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn shares fell after the company presented a lower than expected second quarter profit and said it still saw negative sales and earnings trends in the second half.
At 1110 GMT the share was six crowns lower at 288 crowns.
"The report was not too good. They still see negative earnings trends for 1997," a trader said.
"At the same time you don't know how much (new chief executive and president) Fred Hassan has taken on costs. It's easy to add some extra on costs when you are new."

P&U, created by the merger of Pharmacia of Sweden and U.S. Upjohn in 1995, posted a 33 percent fall in earnings per share (EPS) to US$0.34 before nonrecurring items, while analysts in a Reuters poll expected $0.36 EPS.
P&U said it would take a charge in the third quarter of 1997 of 10 to 16 cents a share for its Biotech merger.
"It's a bit negative that they are taking a charge (of 10-16 cents a share) for the Biotech merger," a trader said.
